headline: ChatGPT 6 beats Gemini hands-down in 5 daily routines, free tier gets Luna
summary: OpenAI's new GPT-6 model, now available on the free tier, offers an Intelligent UI with interactive elements like checklists, quizzes, and flashcards, giving it a significant edge over Gemini's plain text responses in everyday tasks.
details: OpenAI has rolled out GPT-6 to its free tier, offering the Luna model, while paid users get GPT-6 Sol. This update introduces Intelligent UI, enabling the creation of interactive elements like charts and checklists. Meanwhile, Google downgraded Gemini's free tier to 3.5 Flash-Lite.

In a test of daily schedule planning, ChatGPT generated a proper checklist with tick circles and a reset button. Gemini, however, only provided a plain text list with non-tappable brackets. When a call time changed, ChatGPT's interactive list updated seamlessly, while Gemini again offered only plain text.

For a multiple-choice quiz on Android privacy, ChatGPT presented tappable options that changed color with feedback and a running score, feeling like a mini-app. Gemini, in contrast, output a long block of unhelpful HTML code.

When asked for Spanish greeting flashcards, ChatGPT's interactive tool allowed users to tap to reveal answers and mark themselves right or wrong, with a final score. Gemini attempted to build a web app, but its button failed to load, redirecting to a Google sign-in page.

A carry-on packing checklist for a three-day trip saw ChatGPT categorize items with individual counters, "Check all" buttons, and an overall progress bar. Gemini also provided checkboxes but listed all items in one long column with categories preceding each.

For a numerical task ranking cereal box value, both AI correctly identified the best value. ChatGPT displayed clear colored bars and a ranking, while Gemini's chart had three almost identical white bars, requiring users to read the numbers.

ChatGPT wasn't flawless; it made errors in a phone plan comparison. Gemini, on the other hand, excelled at scheduled routines like daily news briefs and successfully built a Google Sheets habit tracker.

Despite minor setbacks, the overall comparison highlights GPT-6's superior interactive capabilities directly within the chat interface. For users seeking dynamic and engaging tools, ChatGPT's latest model is the clear frontrunner.

headline_marked: Major European carriers [[team up for direct satellite program]] to rival Starlink
headline: Major European carriers team up for direct satellite program to rival Starlink
summary: Deutsche Telekom, Orange, Telefónica, and Vodafone are considering a joint bid for spectrum to support a European direct-to-device satellite service, aiming for universal coverage.
details: Deutsche Telekom, Orange, Telefónica, and Vodafone have signed a letter of intent to jointly bid for spectrum. This initiative aims to support European direct-to-device satellite competition against SpaceX's Starlink. Their goal is to achieve universal coverage in underserved areas and strengthen public network resilience.

The four telecom companies plan to establish key ground network infrastructure and coordination functions within Europe. They will not directly invest in a satellite constellation; this will be provided by a separate, yet-to-be-selected satellite partner. This approach combines European governance with proven satellite technology.

This move follows a similar collaboration in the US earlier this year, where AT&T, T-Mobile, and Verizon announced plans to combine spectrum for satellite services. The EU is also considering reserving part of the 2 GHz band for local satellite companies, a proposal criticized by SpaceX.
caption:
Four major European mobile carriers are joining forces to create a direct-to-device satellite program. They aim to rival SpaceX's Starlink for universal coverage across Europe.
